Notes: One of the best-studied examples of Müllerian mimicry; geographic races converge on similar warning patterns.
Key publication(s): Joron et al. 2006; Baxter et al. 2008

Notes: White-banded forms of H. cydno resemble sympatric H. sapho.
Yellow-banded H. cydno alithea resembles sympatric H. eleuchia in western Ecuador.
Some H. timareta populations are nearly identical in warning pattern to sympatric H. melpomene.
Key publication(s): Giraldo et al. 2008; Heliconius Genome Consortium 2012

Notes: H. numata morph f. silvana closely resembles Melinaea ludovica ludovica.
Several H. numata morphs mimic forms of M. marsaeus.
Key publication(s): Joron et al. 2006; Jones et al. 2013

Notes: H. numata f. tarapotensis closely resembles a sympatric form of M. menophilus.
Mimetic female P. polytes resemble the toxic common rose; males and some female morphs are non-mimetic.
Female H. misippus are polymorphic and imitate different colour morphs of D. chrysippus.
Dark-form females of P. glaucus resemble the chemically defended pipevine swallowtail.
The black swallowtail resembles the pipevine swallowtail; dorsal resemblance is especially strong in females.
L. lorquini is palatable and resembles the moderately unpalatable A. bredowii.
Historically treated as Batesian mimicry, but viceroys can themselves be unpalatable.
The spicebush swallowtail belongs to the North American B. philenor mimicry complex.
